monthly_review.summary: You've shifted toward higher-intensity running this month, with notable gains in pace and cadence but reduced aerobic volume and efficiency compared to last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Your Zone 4 time increased from 3% to 21% of total HR distribution — a dramatic 18-point jump indicating a strong recent shift into threshold work, likely contributing to your faster average pace but at the cost of aerobic base maintenance.

goal_tracker.message: You need 22.3 more km across 5 remaining sessions — averaging 4.5 km per session — to match last month’s volume. Prioritize consistency: aim for one 6–7 km run and four 4–5 km runs.

insights.title: Efficiency declined despite faster pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency dropped from 13.42 to 13.19 km/hr per bpm, meaning you’re expending more HR effort per unit speed — consistent with increased time in Z3–Z4 (55% combined this month vs 22% last month) and lower Z1/Z2 volume (52% vs 79%).

insights.title: Threshold emphasis without Z1 recovery balance
insights.body: Z4 now accounts for 21% of HR time (up from 3%), yet Z1 fell from 36% to 20% — suggesting insufficient low-intensity recovery or warm-up/cool-down volume, which may impair fatigue resilience and long-term aerobic development.

insights.title: Cadence improved but vertical oscillation spiked under effort
insights.body: Cadence rose +4 spm (146 → 150), yet during the 7:03/km effort on 2026-06-04, vertical oscillation jumped to 9.2 cm — 1.6 cm above your monthly average (7.7 cm) — indicating less economical form at faster paces.

insights.title: High-intensity density without compensatory recovery
insights.body: Three runs on 2026-06-04 (including a 7:03/km effort at 159 bpm) occurred within <24 hours of a 10 km run — yet avg HR remained elevated (144 bpm) and aerobic TE dropped — suggesting accumulated fatigue is masking true recovery capacity.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a strict 5 km Zone 2 effort (HR ≤135 bpm), focusing on relaxed breathing and stride smoothness — use the 2026-06-04 9:32/km run (HR 137, VO2 max 37.0) as your Z2 upper limit reference.
recommendations.reason: To rebuild Z1/Z2 volume and restore aerobic efficiency — your current Z1+Z2 share (52%) is well below last month's 79%, and your lowest recent HR was 136 bpm (2026-06-04, 9:32/km).

recommendations.action: Insert a 15-minute post-run mobility routine after every run this week, emphasizing hip flexor release and glute activation — especially after any run where vertical oscillation exceeded 8.5 cm (e.g., 2026-06-04’s 9.2 cm effort).
recommendations.reason: Elevated vertical oscillation correlates with inefficiency and excess braking forces; targeted mobility can reduce ground contact time (currently averaging 312 ms) and improve stride economy.

recommendations.action: Replace one midweek run with a 30-minute brisk walk (HR 110–120 bpm) — using your Garmin’s 'All-Day Stress' or 'Recovery Time' metric to confirm readiness before resuming running.
recommendations.reason: Your recent high-Z3/Z4 load and declining aerobic TE (2.4 vs 2.7) signal need for active recovery — and your lowest recorded HR was 136 bpm, confirming no true Z1 effort has been logged recently.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish foundational endurance by prioritizing time-in-zone over pace, restoring Z1/Z2 volume, and reinforcing efficient movement patterns — all while protecting against overreaching from recent threshold work.
suggested_sessions: 4 km progressive run: first 2 km Z2, last 2 km Z3 (HR 140–148 bpm)
